title: McLeans Pass & the Stargate Tunnel
lede: An 11 km return walk on fire trail and track from Moffitts Trail to McLeans Pass, through pagoda country to the Stargate Tunnel and its tree ferns.
description: An 11 km return walk on fire trail and track from the campsite at the junction of Moffitts Trail and the Bicentennial Trail, near Ben Bullen, to McLeans Pass and the Stargate Tunnel, a walk-through sandstone tunnel among the pagodas of Gardens of Stone National Park.
hero_alt: Rounded grey sandstone pagodas rising out of the bush under a sky of white cloud, with ridges fading into the distance

card.image_alt: Looking along a tall, narrow sandstone tunnel with a sandy floor towards daylight and tree ferns at the far end
card.blurb: Out through pagoda country to McLeans Pass, then walk through the Stargate Tunnel into a gully full of tree ferns.

facts.label: Region
facts.value: Gardens of Stone, near Ben Bullen

facts.label: Distance
facts.value: About 11 km return, or about 7 km return from the south

facts.label: Walk type
facts.value: Track (fire trail and faint track); Return

facts.label: Highlights
facts.value: McLeans Pass, the Stargate Tunnel, pagodas, tree ferns

intro: East of Baal Bone Gap, the plateau breaks up into a maze of sandstone pagodas. At McLeans Pass, below Mount McLean, a tunnel runs right through the rock. Walk through the Stargate Tunnel and you come out into a damp, sheltered gully full of tree ferns.

getting_there.intro: The walk starts at the campsite at the junction of Moffitts Trail and the Bicentennial Trail (Ben Bullen GR 289 179). Get there via Ben Bullen.

options.heading: Moffitts Trail
options.text:
From Ben Bullen, head out on Moffitts Trail (also signposted as Ben Bullen Trail) to the campsite at the Bicentennial Trail junction.

In a 2WD you might only get as far as the start of the [Mercurys Boot](/mercurys-boot/) walk, so be ready to walk the rest of the way to the campsite.

options.heading: Bicentennial Trail
options.text: Coming from the south, you can start on the Bicentennial Trail at Ben Bullen GR 298 163, where the route turns north-east towards McLeans Pass. This cuts about 2 km off each way, making it about 7 km return.

getting_there.note: Fire trail conditions change quickly after rain. Check the current NPWS alerts for Gardens of Stone National Park before you go.

walk_intro:
The route follows the Bicentennial Trail south-east and then south from the campsite for about 2 km, then turns north-east onto a track that climbs to McLeans Pass. It's about 5.5 km each way on fire trail and track. Come back the same way.

The track isn't used much, so it may be faint in places.

stops.heading: Moffitts Trail campsite
stops.text: Start at the campsite at the junction of Moffitts Trail and the Bicentennial Trail (Ben Bullen GR 289 179). Follow the Bicentennial Trail south-east, then south.

stops.heading: Turn north-east
stops.text:
About 2 km from the start, at Ben Bullen GR 298 163, leave the Bicentennial Trail and turn north-east onto the track towards Mount McLean. This is also where you start if you've come in from the south.

The track isn't used much, so it can be faint in places. Keep an eye on the map.

stops.heading: Pagoda country
stops.text: As you get closer to Mount McLean, the bush opens up and rounded grey sandstone pagodas rise out of the scrub, with views out over the ridges beyond.
stops.image_alt: Rounded grey sandstone pagodas rising out of the bush under a sky of white cloud, with ridges fading into the distance
stops.caption: Pagodas near Mount McLean

stops.heading: McLeans Pass
stops.text:
McLeans Pass is a way up through the pagodas just east of Mount McLean, and the turnaround point for this walk.

From the pass you can keep exploring the plateau as you wish. It's possible to get out to Point Cameron (and down from it), but that means multiple steep drop-offs and lots of scrub, so it's only for experienced off-track walkers.

stops.heading: The Stargate Tunnel
stops.text: Just below the pass, the Stargate Tunnel runs right through the sandstone. It's tall and narrow, with a sandy floor, and you can walk through it towards the light at the far end.
stops.image_alt: Looking along a tall, narrow sandstone tunnel with a sandy floor towards daylight and tree ferns at the far end
stops.caption: Looking through the Stargate Tunnel

stops.heading: The tree fern gully
stops.text: On the other side is a sheltered gully between sheer sandstone walls, full of tree ferns and bracken. It's a good place to stop for lunch in the shade.
stops.image_alt: Tall tree ferns and bright green bracken in a narrow gully between high, honeycombed sandstone cliffs, under a blue sky
stops.caption: Tree ferns in the gully by the Stargate Tunnel

stops.heading: Back to the car
stops.text: Retrace your steps to the camping ground on Moffitts Trail.

map.alt: Topographic map showing the route from the Moffitts Trail camping ground south-east, then north-east along the Wolgan State Forest boundary to McLeans Pass and the Stargate Tunnel
map.caption: Approximate route in orange. Base map: Ben Bullen 8931-4S and Cullen Bullen 8931-3N topographic maps, joined at the black line.

tips.heading: Navigation
tips.text: The route is on fire trail and track, but the track isn't used much and may be faint in places, and there are no signs to McLeans Pass or the Stargate Tunnel. Carry a map and compass or the GPX on your phone, and know how to use them. Going beyond the pass to Point Cameron is off-track, with steep drop-offs and lots of scrub.

tips.heading: Pagodas and cliffs
tips.text: The pagodas and the walls around the tunnel are high and sheer. Take care on the rock, especially when it's wet.

tips.heading: Water
tips.text: Carry all the water you'll need. Don't rely on finding any on the way.

tips.heading: Respect the Country
tips.text: Look, but don't touch. Leave no trace.

tips.heading: Tell someone
tips.text: Leave your plans with someone, and think about carrying a PLB. There's very little phone coverage out there.
